rounds.proof_sketch: The mutation changes threshold from M >= 1024 to M >= 1023. With fixed input shape B=[4096, 4096], M=4096 is constant. Original: 4096 >= 1024 → true (optimized kernel). Mutant: 4096 >= 1023 → true (optimized kernel). Both evaluate identically since 4096 >> 1024 > 1023. The difference only matters when M ∈ [1023, 1023], which is unreachable under fixed shapes.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation modifies a conditional threshold that selects between two CUDA kernels based on the matrix width M. With the fixed input specification where B has shape [4096, 4096], M is always 4096. Both the original condition (M >= 1024) and mutated condition (M >= 1023) evaluate to true when M = 4096. Therefore, both versions always select the optimized kernel for this fixed configuration. Since kernel selection depends solely on the dimension M (not tensor values), no value-level input variation can cause the mutant to behave differently. The mutation would only be distinguishable if M could be exactly 1023, which violates the fixed-shape contract.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable under the fixed-shape contract. The mutation affects kernel selection based on dimension M, which is fixed at 4096. Both conditions (M >= 1024 and M >= 1023) evaluate identically for M = 4096. To kill this mutant would require changing M to 1023, which violates the testing contract that shapes are fixed.
rounds.recommendations: For mutation testing of threshold-based kernel selection, ensure test suites include configurations where M equals or is near the threshold values (1023, 1024 in this case). When fixed shapes place dimensions far from thresholds, such mutations become semantically equivalent and should be classified as equivalent mutants or the test harness should support parameterized shape testing for threshold-sensitive code paths.
